attempts.settings_or_prompt:
Use case: historical-scene
Asset type: 4:5 editorial social-media image for Sabiduría de Bolsillo, Day 1 single-image experiment
Primary request: Create an original, visually arresting editorial illustration inspired by Anna Atkins's 1843 cyanotype work, centered on a single delicate British algae specimen making a white photogram silhouette against rich Prussian blue sensitized paper. The image should immediately communicate scientific discovery, sunlight, paper, and botanical form without pretending to reproduce a specific surviving plate.
Scene/backdrop: a restrained 1840s British botanical worktable at the edge of frame, with the cyanotype sheet as the dominant subject; subtle glass contact frame and soft daylight, period-appropriate materials only.
Subject: one intricate algae specimen in crisp pale silhouette on blue paper; no identifiable real person.
Style/medium: polished editorial illustration with tactile photographic-paper grain, historically grounded, elegant and contemporary enough for a cultural-history account.
Composition/framing: portrait 4:5; the cyanotype occupies most of the frame; generous clean dark-blue negative space in the upper third and lower edge for a later code-rendered Spanish headline and small brand mark.
Lighting/mood: cool Prussian blue, sunlight glow at one edge, curious and contemplative.
Color palette: Prussian blue, cyan, warm off-white, tiny muted brass accents.
Constraints: no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark; do not imitate or copy a specific museum plate; no anachronistic tools; no camera; no printed typography; no hands; accurate botanical silhouette rather than fantasy coral.
